title: Simplify deeply nested conditional pricing logic
description: A pricing-calculation function has five levels of nested if/else branching handling combinations of customer tier, promo codes, and regional tax rules, making it difficult to verify and extend. Refactor it into an equivalent, flatter implementation (guard clauses and/or a small rule table) with identical output for all existing test cases.
acceptanceCriteria: Maximum nesting depth in the refactored function is reduced to at most two levels.
All existing pricing test cases produce byte-identical output before and after the refactor.
No new pricing rule or behavior is introduced beyond what the original nested logic implemented.
The refactored function is demonstrably easier to extend, evidenced by an added test for one new tier/promo combination requiring only a small, localized change.
verificationMethod: test-suite: run the full existing pricing test suite unchanged, plus one added combination test, and diff-analysis to confirm a behavior-preserving structural change.
groundTruth: The nested conditionals are replaced with early-return guard clauses and/or a lookup table keyed by (tier, promoActive, region), producing exactly the same price for every input the original branching handled.
